author: marici.Strominger

scope.strength: symbolic and finite exact Diophantine theorem

checks.statement: at g=2 the unique odd positive root is d=5
for every g>=3 the obstruction is genuinely quadratic in d
the discriminant lies strictly above S(g)^2 for g>=3
the discriminant lies below (S(g)+1)^2 for g>=67
the only square discriminant for 3<=g<=66 occurs at g=6
the two roots at g=6 are nonintegral
P(g,d)=0 on g>=2 and integral d implies (g,d)=(2,5)
checks.detail: g=2 is linear; g=3..66 audited; g>=67 trapped between consecutive squares

checks.statement: the odd-core Diophantine lemma has the unique admissible solution (2,5)

verdict: The odd-core obstruction P is linear at g=2 with root d=5. For g>=3 it is quadratic in d. Its discriminant is trapped strictly between S(g)^2 and (S(g)+1)^2 for every g>=67. Exact inspection of 3<=g<=66 finds one square discriminant, at g=6, whose roots 17/3 and 37/3 are nonintegral. Therefore P(g,d)=0 has the unique integral solution (g,d)=(2,5), proving that the only odd low-grade kernel exception is (g,q)=(2,7).
